gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Epson EpiqVision Flex CO-W01, one of the two projectors it showed, plays only Motion JPEG AVI 1.0 video from a USB drive (at most 1280×720 and under 2 GB), so ordinary MP4/H.264 movie files will not play from a USB stick without a Wi-Fi or HDMI source.
standout_why: I compared against the laserco.freshdesk.com FAQ (it lists MP4/AVI/MOV H.264 for a different Laser Corp projector), nexttools.net (only general advice about MHL and USB-C-to-HDMI adapters, no file types), innovativeprojector.com (no file types, no named models apart from its own brand) and the Notebookcheck ZIP Pro review. None gives the Epson CO-W01's USB file-type limit. None says which phones can drive the Aurzen ZIP projectors over USB-C (DP Alt Mode). ChatGPT's answer offered 'USB drive with downloaded movies' as a path and showed the CO-W01 at $399.99, but never said that this projector's USB playback excludes MP4.
decides: If the shopper picks ChatGPT's 'USB drive with downloaded movies' or 'projector should play movies by itself' option, Epson's own guide rules the CO-W01 out unless the files are converted to Motion JPEG AVI. It works offline only from an HDMI source such as a laptop or Blu-ray player. For the Aurzen ZIP family, a wired phone connection works only if the phone has DisplayPort Alt Mode. Aurzen says budget and older phones 'rarely support' it. The CastPlay Pro dongle needs no Wi-Fi or router, but it still needs a DP Alt Mode source.

findings.label: Video files it plays from a USB drive (PC Free)
findings.value: Only Motion JPEG .avi (AVI 1.0), PCM or ADPCM audio, at most 1280×720, under 2 GB
findings.source_title: Supported PC Free File Types (CO-W01 User's Guide, cpd62244)
findings.note: Epson's search index titles doc ID cpd62244 'CO-W01 User's Guide'. The page itself shows no product name. MP4, MOV and H.264 are not listed, so a typical downloaded movie will not play from USB.

findings.label: Still images it shows from a USB drive (PC Free)
findings.value: .jpg up to 8192×8192 (no CMYK, progressive or JPEG 2000); .bmp, .gif and .png up to 1280×800 (no animated GIF, no interlaced GIF or PNG)
findings.source_title: Supported PC Free File Types (CO-W01 User's Guide, cpd62244)
findings.note: Same Epson guide page as above.

findings.label: Offline video source and price
findings.value: Built-in HDMI port (Epson suggests plugging in a streaming device); $399.99 on epson.com
findings.source_title: Epson EpiqVision Flex CO-W01 Portable Projector | Epson US
findings.note: The page says 'built-in HDMI port and speaker' and tells buyers to connect their 'preferred streaming solution' to HDMI. Streaming apps need a 'wireless network connection of 5 Mbps or faster'. Box contents: projector, power cable, remote, batteries, Quick Start Guide. No streaming stick or HDMI cable included.

findings.label: Wired video input
findings.value: USB-C 3.0 video in with DP Alt Mode only (no HDMI port in the spec list); latency up to 40 ms; wireless casting via AirLink, AirPlay P2P, DLNA, Google Cast and Miracast
findings.source_title: Aurzen Zip Pro tri-fold 1080p projector: Superb pocketable design (Notebookcheck, David Chien)
findings.note: This is reviewer data, not Aurzen's: aurzen.com's ZIP Pro page returned HTTP 429 on three tries. Per Notebookcheck's spec table, the lower USB-C port is for charging and S/PDIF. The review lists 'No built-in streaming services' as a con and does not mention USB-drive playback.

findings.label: Which source devices work
findings.value: The source's USB-C port must support DisplayPort Alt Mode. Aurzen guarantees Samsung Galaxy S/Note/Z (S8 and newer), USB-C MacBooks, iPad Pro and Thunderbolt 3/4 laptops. It lists Nintendo Switch and Switch OLED with pass-through charging. It says budget or older NA/EU phones 'rarely support' DP Alt Mode.
findings.source_title: Aurzen CastPlay Pro Wireless USB-C Dongle Help Center
findings.note: Aurzen names the Galaxy A53 and Pixel 6a as phones to check, without saying whether they work. The page ties the dongle to the ZIP projector and names no other model.

findings.label: Network needed
findings.value: None: 'no Wi-Fi, apps, or software installation required' (direct peer-to-peer link)
findings.source_title: Aurzen CastPlay Pro Wireless USB-C Dongle Help Center
findings.note: Aurzen also says DRM content from Netflix and Disney+ can be streamed through it. The page does not mention HDCP.
